questions.text: When a change in level occurs on an accessible route, what does BP 344 require unless a dropped sidewalk, curb ramp, elevator, or other mechanical device serves it?

options.text: A stair without an alternative route

questions.rationale: Correct answer: A ramp. This is directly supported by BP 344 2024 Revised IRR, Accessible Ramps.

questions.text: What minimum clear width is required for an accessible ramp?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 1200 mm. This is directly supported by BP 344 2024 Revised IRR, Accessible Ramps.

questions.text: What is the general maximum gradient for accessible ramps?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Not steeper than 1:20. This is directly supported by BP 344 2024 Revised IRR, Accessible Ramps.
questions.explanation: 400–600 mm AFF is explicitly stated in BP 344 Sec. 6 so a fallen user can activate the alarm.

questions.text: For accessible ramps longer than 10.50 m, what intermediate landing length is required?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 1800 mm minimum. This is directly supported by BP 344 2024 Revised IRR, Accessible Ramps.
questions.explanation: The two-level counter requires a 750 mm lower level with 700 mm knee clearance per BP 344 Sec. 14.

questions.text: At what two heights must handrails be installed above accessible ramps and stairs?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 900 mm and 700 mm. This is directly supported by BP 344 2024 Revised IRR, Handrails.
questions.explanation: 3% × 500 = 15 spaces at 900 × 1200 mm each under the 2024 IRR flat-rate rule.

questions.text: The Right to Health (RA 7277 Sec. 23) requires accessible hospital toilets. What are the minimum clear internal dimensions of the accessible WC cubicle under BP 344 2024 Revised IRR?

options.text: 2000 mm wide x 2000 mm deep, with a 900 mm door that slides only
1500 mm wide x 1800 mm deep, with a 750 mm door that swings inward
1800 mm wide x 1800 mm deep, with a 900 mm door that swings outward or slides
1800 mm wide x 2250 mm deep, with a 900 mm door that swings out or slides

questions.rationale: Correct answer: C — 1800 mm x 1800 mm minimum clear internal area with a 900 mm outward-swinging or sliding door. Source verbatim (BP 344 2024 Revised IRR, Appendix A, item 1, PDF p.36 line 1143): 'A minimum area of 1800 mm x 1800 mm.' The 2250 mm depth in option D is not in the source and is the documented error being corrected.
questions.explanation: 1800 × 2250 mm clear with a 900 mm out-swinging or sliding door is the BP 344 Sec. 6 minimum.

questions.text: What minimum clear width is required for all doors?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 900 mm. This is directly supported by BP 344 2024 Revised IRR, Doors.
questions.explanation: Maximum 3 Hz, minimum 2 candelas, white lens per BP 344 Sec. 17.8 — flash rate is a ceiling, not a floor.

questions.text: An architect is designing a grab bar for the side wall of an accessible WC cubicle. The WC seat height is 450 mm AFF. At what height above finished floor should the horizontal grab bar be mounted?

options.text: 900 mm AFF — matching the lever handle and handrail height standard
300 mm AFF — as stated in the BP 344 grab bar specification
750 mm AFF — 300 mm above the 450 mm WC seat height
760 mm AFF — 300 mm above a 460 mm WC seat height

questions.rationale: Correct answer: C — 750 mm AFF. The WC seat is 450 mm AFF and the grab bar sits 300 mm above the seat top, so 450 + 300 = 750 mm AFF. Source verbatim: 'The height of toilet seat shall be 450 mm.' (BP 344 2024 Revised IRR, PDF p.37 line 1199) and 'Both grab bars shall be installed 300 mm high from the top of the toilet seat to the top of the grab bars.' (PDF p.36 lines 1153-1154). Option D uses the erroneous 460 mm seat height, which is not in the source.
questions.explanation: Grab bar height = WC seat height + 300 mm per BP 344 Sec. 6; 460 + 300 = 760 mm AFF.

questions.text: What opening force limit applies to interior door closer devices, except stated exclusions?

options.text: No limit is stated for interior door closers

questions.rationale: Correct answer: Not more than 2.0 kg. This is directly supported by BP 344 2024 Revised IRR, Doors.
questions.explanation: BP 344 mandates at least one accessible toilet per floor — the elevator argument does not satisfy this requirement.

questions.text: Where should door handles, pulls, latches, and lever-type locksets be centered?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 900 mm above floor finish level. This is directly supported by BP 344 2024 Revised IRR, Doors.
questions.explanation: Pool transfer wall = 450 mm AFF; transfer space = 1500 × 1500 mm per BP 344 Sec. 1.

questions.text: What minimum clear width is required for accessible staircases?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 1.50 m. This is directly supported by BP 344 2024 Revised IRR, Accessible Stairs.
questions.explanation: Accessible workstation per BP 344 Sec. 15: 900 mm wide, 700 × 480 mm knee clearance, 1500 × 1500 mm turning space alongside.

questions.text: A senior architect reviews a transit terminal design and finds the accessible parking stalls are 3500 mm wide with a 1500 mm shared aisle, located at the far end of the lot. Which two non-compliances must be corrected under BP 344 2024 Revised IRR?

options.text: Stall must be 4000 mm x 5000 mm (the extra 1500 mm width forms the access aisle, not a separate strip); stalls must be nearest the accessible entrance
Stall must be 4000 mm wide with a separate 1800 mm access aisle; stalls must be nearest the accessible entrance
Stall must be 4000 mm wide with a separate 1800 mm access aisle; vertical clearance must be 2300 mm
Stall must be 5000 mm wide with a separate 1800 mm access aisle; stalls must be nearest the accessible entrance

questions.rationale: Correct answer: A. BP 344 specifies a single accessible parking slot of 4000 mm x 5000 mm; the additional 1500 mm width (versus an average slot) IS the access aisle that accommodates wheelchair passage — it is not a separate 1800 mm strip. Stalls must also be on the shortest accessible route to the accessible entrance, so the far-end location is a non-compliance. Source verbatim (BP 344 2024 Revised IRR, PDF p.7 lines 283-285): 'A minimum width of 4000 mm and a length of 5000 mm. The additional 1500 mm width, in comparison to the average parking slot, is intended to ensure that the adjacent pathway adequately accommodates wheelchair passage.'
questions.explanation: Stall width 4000 mm, access aisle 1800 mm, and nearest-to-entrance location are all mandatory per BP 344.
